newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Khrunichev gets $35 mln loan for space projects.
newsitem.headline: Khrunichev gets $35 mln loan for space projects.

text.p: Russia's International Moscow Bank signed a $35 million credit agreement with the Khrunichev Space Centre (KSC) on Monday, helping to create 100,000 new jobs.
The bank will extend Khrunichev the money for space projects over the next two years.

The space centre's director general Anatoly Kiselyev told reporters the money would allow its sub-contractors to buy materials and equipment needed for new rockets. "The loan will help give jobs to about 100,000 people," he said.
He said the space centre had launched six Proton rockets last year and planned 12 launches during 1997. It hoped to earn $1.5 billion by the year 2000 from launching Western-made satellites.
Viktor Gerashchenko, head of the International Moscow Bank, said Khrunichev had a big potential.
Kiselyev said part of the loan would be used to build two ground stations for receiving Iridium LLC satellite signals and using them in Russia's telephone network.
The Iridium consortium comprises 17 companies including Motorola, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp, Pacific Electric Wire & Cable Co Ltd of Taiwan and Raytheon Co.
